glosses: … and that was the last of it
patterns.usage_note: Emphatic colloquial variant of 〜たきり (the small っ is what adds the emphasis), attached to the plain past form of a verb: it marks that action as the last time, with nothing following it. The second clause is almost always negative or otherwise describes a state that has simply persisted ever since, and the pattern typically carries worry, resignation, or mild complaint rather than neutral reporting. Reserve it for speech and casual writing; 〜たきり is the neutral form and 〜たまま is the choice when you mean a state left unchanged rather than an event never repeated.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]は部屋[へや]に駆[か]け込[こ]んだっきり出[で]て来[こ]ない。
examples.english: My brother bolted into his room and hasn't come out since.

examples.ruby: 先輩[せんぱい]は卒業[そつぎょう]の日[ひ]に見[み]かけたっきりだ。
examples.english: The last I ever saw of my senpai was on graduation day.

examples.ruby: 借[か]りた本[ほん]は最初[さいしょ]の章[しょう]を読[よ]んだっきり、開[ひら]いていない。
examples.english: I read the first chapter of the book I borrowed and haven't opened it since.
